fixes.explanation: Aaron is a fair guess, friend. He's Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and the LORD told Moses to bring him near to serve as priest (Exodus 28:1). But in this verse Moses says the command is what "…the LORD has commanded…" (Numbers 30:1). Aaron isn't named here at all.

Joshua is a fair guess, friend. He's called Moses' assistant (Exodus 24:13), and after Moses died, the LORD spoke to Joshua about leading the people across the Jordan (Joshua 1:1–2). But this verse doesn't mention him. Moses says, "This is what the LORD has commanded…" (Numbers 30:1). So the command comes from the LORD, and Moses is just the one passing it on.

True, baker. The text says that when her father "…says nothing to her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand." (Numbers 30:4). Silence counts for something here. It's like a friend texting "We still on for Saturday?" and you read it and never answer. Everybody figures you're in.

I get why an offering comes to mind, friend. But this verse doesn't ask her for one. It says, "The LORD will absolve her because her father has prohibited her." (Numbers 30:5). That's the whole answer, with no offering in sight.
